findings.claim: The Python template string in the issue-body heredoc uses `\`` (backslash + backtick) throughout as inline-code delimiters (lines 394, 405, 410, 414, 428, 438, 445, 447 of release-gate.yml). In Python 3.12 (the ubuntu-24.04 default) each `\`` is a deprecated invalid escape sequence; Python emits a DeprecationWarning per occurrence to stderr and stores both characters — literal backslash + backtick — in the string value. In CommonMark (GitHub's issue-body renderer) `\`` is a backslash escape that renders as a visible backtick glyph, not as a code-span delimiter. Consequently all intended inline-code spans in the rendered issue body (`` `vX.Y.Z` ``, `` `SCP-EREL-001` ``, `` `policies/VERSIONING.md` ``, `` `administration:write` ``, `` `.github/workflows/release-gate.yml` `` etc.) appear as backtick-text-backtick visible characters without `<code>` styling. This diverges from the canary-replay.yml pattern the step claims to mirror: canary-replay.yml uses plain `` ` `` inside the same triple-quoted template (line 159 et seq.) — correct Python, correct Markdown.
findings.evidence: release-gate.yml lines 394 (`- Candidate tag: \`__TAG__\``), 405 (`\`scp-tag-protection-v\``), 410 (`\`SCP-EREL-001\``), 414 (`\`policies/VERSIONING.md\``), 428 (`\`v<X>.<Y+1>.0\``), 438 (`\`administration:write\``), 445 (`\`policies/VERSIONING.md\``), 447 (`\`docs/DECISIONS.md\``); Python language reference §2.4.1 — only listed escape sequences (\ n, t, r, \, ', " etc.) are valid; bpo-27364 / PEP 461 — invalid escapes emit DeprecationWarning in 3.6+; Python 3.13 release notes — invalid escape sequences promoted to SyntaxWarning; CommonMark spec §6.1 — backslash before ASCII punctuation is a backslash escape, output is the literal punctuation character with no further processing (no code-span semantics); canary-replay.yml line 159 `- HEAD on \`main\` at the time of this replay.` — plain backtick, no backslash.
findings.impact: (1) DeprecationWarning noise on stderr for every push:tags failure run in which the issue body is composed; non-blocking at Python 3.12 but will become SyntaxWarning on Python 3.13 and may become SyntaxError on a future runner image upgrade, silently breaking the issue-body composition step. (2) All inline-code references in the rendered issue body are aesthetically degraded — readable but not styled as code, reducing triage ergonomics. (3) Pattern divergence from canary-replay.yml creates a maintainability inconsistency: the two workflows claim to follow the same body-composition pattern but differ in a way that will widen over time.
findings.mitigation: Replace every `\`` in the triple-quoted template string with a plain backtick `` ` ``. Triple-quoted Python strings do not require backtick escaping; the substitution is a one-to-one find-and-replace across the eight affected lines. The plain-backtick form is already the correct pattern in canary-replay.yml. No logic change required.

findings.claim: The auto-issue step condition `if: failure() && github.event_name == 'push'` causes the step to fire whenever ANY prior step in the job has failed on a push:tags event — including infrastructure failures unrelated to gate evaluation (actions/checkout network error, pip install PyPI unavailability, Python smoke-test failure at line 111). A transient runner failure would open a `release-gate-violation` issue titled `[release-gate-violation] tag vX.Y.Z failed validation`, implying a compliance gate violation when the actual cause is an infra fault. The tag may satisfy all gate invariants. This is a semantic false-positive: the issue title says 'failed validation' but no SCP-EREL-001 annotation would exist in the workflow run. The analogous step in canary-replay.yml gates on a specific step output (`if: steps.replay.outputs.exit_code != '0'`) rather than the broad `failure()`, restricting issue creation to the detection logic's own exit code and excluding infra failures upstream of the detection step.
findings.evidence: release-gate.yml line 345: `if: failure() && github.event_name == 'push'`; GitHub Actions docs — `failure()` returns true if any previous step or job in the workflow failed or was cancelled; release-gate.yml lines 95-111 — Checkout and Install steps precede gate-logic steps; canary-replay.yml line 104-105: `if: steps.replay.outputs.exit_code != '0'` — step-specific sentinel, does not fire on upstream infra failures.
findings.impact: Infrequent false-positive `release-gate-violation` issues on transient runner infra failures. Operator must inspect the workflow run to distinguish gate failures (EREL-001 annotations present) from infra failures (no EREL-001 annotations). Triage workload is low since the distinction is clear, but the issue title 'failed validation' is misleading for infra-failure cases and may cause confusion for a second maintainer unfamiliar with the distinction.
findings.mitigation: Add an explicit step-level output on the gate-check steps to signal gate-logic failure: after the last gate-check step (Release-gate verdict), add a sentinel step that runs only on success and sets `gate_passed=true`; then condition the auto-issue step on the absence of that output (`if: steps.verdict.conclusion == 'failure' && github.event_name == 'push'`), where `steps.verdict.conclusion` is `'failure'` only if the verdict step itself or a gate step failed. Lower-effort alternative: in the workflow comment and the triage checklist, explicitly state that absence of SCP-EREL-001 annotations indicates an infra failure, not a gate violation — the existing checklist item 'Reviewed the SCP-EREL-001 annotations on the workflow run' already provides this signal; add one sentence: 'If no SCP-EREL-001 annotations are present, this issue is a false positive caused by a runner infra failure — close with label infra-false-positive and re-run the workflow.'

findings.claim: `gh issue list --search "in:title \"${title}\""` relies on GitHub Issues search API double-quoted phrase matching for a title that begins with `[release-gate-violation]`. The GitHub Search API's treatment of square brackets in quoted strings is not explicitly specified in public documentation; square brackets are list notation in some query syntaxes and may affect tokenisation. In the event the API mis-tokenises the quoted title containing `[...]`, the search could return zero results even when a matching open issue exists, causing a duplicate issue to be created for re-runs of the same failed tag. The label filter `--label release-gate-violation` combined with `--state open` provides a fallback de-dup signal during manual triage. Functionally correct in all observed production scenarios using the identical canary-replay.yml pattern.
findings.evidence: release-gate.yml lines 371-377; canary-replay.yml lines 121-127 — identical double-quote-wrapped `in:title` pattern with different title text (week-tag string, no square brackets); GitHub REST API docs for issue search — phrase semantics mentioned for repository search but not explicitly for issues search; pattern verified to fixpoint in 020H.1 canary-replay.yml review.
findings.impact: Potential duplicate-issue creation on workflow re-runs for the same failed tag if the search API does not match the bracketed title as expected. Each duplicate is visible to the operator and closable; no data loss or silent failure.
findings.mitigation: Use a bracket-free search token: `--search "in:title tag ${tag} failed validation"` — the tag substring plus the `release-gate-violation` label and `open` state filter provides sufficient deduplication without relying on bracket-containing phrase matching. This is forward-compat hardening; the current implementation is functionally adequate.

findings.claim: The concurrency group expression `release-gate-${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.dry_run_tag || github.ref }}` resolves to different keys for a workflow_dispatch dry-run and a push event targeting the same tag: `release-gate-v1.0.1` for `workflow_dispatch` with `dry_run_tag=v1.0.1`, and `release-gate-refs/tags/v1.0.1` for a `push:tags` event. These are different keys; they do not serialize against each other. The workflow comment at lines 82-84 asserts `a real push:tags is still serialised against any in-flight dry-run for the same tag` — this assertion is false. Pre-existing from the 020H.3 base slice; not introduced by 020H.3.1. Correctness impact on the new auto-issue step is nil: the step is gated on `github.event_name == 'push'`, so workflow_dispatch dry-runs cannot reach it under any concurrency configuration.
findings.evidence: release-gate.yml lines 82-85: concurrency group expression; GitHub Actions expression evaluation — `inputs.dry_run_tag` for workflow_dispatch = `'v1.0.1'` (truthy, short-circuits); `inputs.dry_run_tag` for push event = empty string (falsy, falls through to `github.ref` = `'refs/tags/v1.0.1'`); `release-gate-v1.0.1` ≠ `release-gate-refs/tags/v1.0.1`; auto-issue step line 345 condition prevents workflow_dispatch from reaching it.
findings.impact: A workflow_dispatch dry-run for `v1.0.1` and a concurrent push of `refs/tags/v1.0.1` run in separate concurrency buckets; both evaluate the same static files deterministically so there is no integrity risk. No impact on the auto-issue step. The incorrect comment is a documentation error only.
findings.mitigation: Correct the concurrency expression to `release-gate-${{ inputs.dry_run_tag || github.ref_name }}`: `github.ref_name` strips the `refs/tags/` prefix, yielding `v1.0.1` for both event types and making the serialisation claim in the comment accurate. Deferred to a future housekeeping slice; pre-existing, no correctness impact on 020H.3.1.
